output.title: Spot duplicate emails before they turn into cleanup work
output.body:
If you run a small business, duplicate emails are worth treating as a workflow question, not a tech puzzle. The real check is simple: do duplicates reach you before you act on them? If they do, the cost is usually wasted review time, inconsistent replies, or cleanup later. That is enough to look at the process. Not enough to automate blindly.

Start with three recent examples. For each one, note where the duplicate came from: a system syncing the same contact twice, the same person sending again, or you copying a thread into another tool. Then sort the duplicates into two groups: must be caught before action, or can be cleaned up later. An invoice or payment request belongs in the first group. A newsletter usually does not. Human approval stays in place for anything involving money or other high-risk decisions.

One practical next step: run a one-week manual test. Put suspicious duplicates into one folder and review them by hand. Count only the repeats, the false positives, and the time your own review takes. If the pattern is messy, that is still useful. It means the next step is a clearer definition of “duplicate,” not a bigger tool. Small problem, small test, no drama.
